recipes.name: Spicy Black Bean Vegetable Soup
ingredients_raw: 2 (15 ounce) cans black beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: In large saucepan, heat oil over medium heat; cook onion, garlic, and carrots, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes or until onion is softened. Add chili powder and cumin; cook, stirring, for 1 minute. Add stock, 1 can of the beans, corn, and pepper; bring to boil.
Meanwhile, in food processor or blender, puree together tomatoes and remaining can of beans; add to pot. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes or until carrots are tender.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Black Bean Vegetable Soup
raw_recipe.description: Half of the black beans in this spicy soup are pureed with tomatoes, the other half are simmered with carrots, onion and kernels of corn.

review.reviewBody: This soup is absolutely delicious! I made a few changes to make it thicker and tastier. I added 3 cloves of garlic, added extra chili powder, added 2.5 cups of chicken broth instead of 4 cups of vegetable stock, added chopped celery (2 stalks) when I added the corn, and used 3 cans of beans instead of 2 (1.5 in the blender and 1.5 as whole beans). I like using the Del Monte Fiesta Corn when making this recipe because the pieces of pepper add a little more spice. All in all, a GREAT soup. I made it for my parents and my 13-year old sister and we ate the entire pot in one sitting. My sister is the pickiest eater ever and she loved it, so that says alot about how good it was. Thanks so much for sharing this with us, DeeDee!

This soup is some of the best I've ever tasted! BUT, after reading a few reviews about it being 'watery' and 'bland', I:
reduced the broth to 2 cups; added an extra can of beans (not pureed); used 2 tsp cumin; 2 cloves of garlic; added 1/3 c cilantro; plus I left out the corn. With a little Greek yogurt (or sour cream) on top... WOW!! Incredible. Thanks for the recipe!

This recipe is wonderful! Usually black bean soup is thick and tastes like nothing, but black beans.
I actually like the boring old black bean soup that I just described, but this recipe is
ten times better! You can taste the onions and carrots and corn. It has wondeful
flavor! I will definitely be making this again. I put a little bit of shredded cheese on
top.

Wonderful soup that can be modified with whatever you have on hand. Per some suggestions cut the broth to 2 cups. I like more texture so I didn’t purée, instead coarsely mashed the tomatoes and two thirds of the 2nd can of beans (for more color use a mixture of beans). Added chopped red pepper, some leftover chopped bacon, and a handful of chopped collards. Ratcheted the spice up a bit with smoky ground chipotle. Served with cornbread … a great Southern dinner on a chilly and rainy day.

Used a frozen diced mirepoix of celery, onions, bell peppers that I had on hand. Substituted some frozen riced butternut squash for the carrots (cuz I had it on hand) Sautéed those together In coconut oil until caramelized to start the soup. Deglazed with the vegetable broth. Added extra garlic. Otherwise followed the recipe. It’s very Very good. Cheap and easy too! For a family with some vegetarians some not, this was a winner with everyone!

This soup is tasty, healthy and fast to make. The 1st time making this, I followed the recipe exactly and it came out very good, but just little bit on the runny side for my taste. From then on, I use only 3 cups of broth. Also I like to add some chopped peppers and celery to the mentioned veggies for more nutrition and a handful of chopped cilantro at the end of simmering for more flavor. And if I am not in hurry I like to simmer the soup for a longer time.

Excellent base recipe. My tweaks: Added 3 cloves garlic, 1 small habanero that I blended with the tomatoes, 2 stalks diced celery, 1 diced green pepper, 1 cup diced chicken breast. Subtracted: corn, 1/2 chili powder. This came out great. Good heat, Very filling.

This was a good soup but was rather bland as written. I more than doubled the amount of chili powder and ground cumin called for. I thought I had vegetable broth but it turned out to be beef broth. It worked just fine. I used my immersion blender to puree the tomatoes and black beans. I also cooked dried black beans rather than use canned.

3 cloves of garlic, extra chili powder & cumin. added 2.5 cups of chicken broth instead of 4 cups of vegetable stock, added chopped celery (2 stalks) when I added the corn, and used 3 cans of beans instead of 2. added a zucchini and about 2 or 3 T of chopped fresh cilantro; rice at end to make it thick.

Use this recipe as a base and customized it to my liking. I added more veggies, such as celery, zucchini & green peppers. I also added egg noodles & Mexican meatless crumbles. I threw all veggies, spices & broth in the crockpot. Cooked on low for 6hrs. I did end up adding more spice than the recipe called for, again I customized it to my liking. After the 6 hrs put the crockpot on warm & added the noodles & crumbles. Soup turned out really good, I did have to add more broth due to the extra ingredients I added. I really enjoyed the soup, topped it off with sour cream & mexican cheese.

Delicious! I put everything together, and just used my immersion blender in the pot to puree it half way! No need to dirty a blender. I liked another person's idea to use some potato instead of three cans of beans, and I thought it was perfect--probably helped thicken it too. I did add extra spice, as others had suggested, and it was great.
It was good. I used a creole seasoning instead of ths recommended spices and chicken bullion and hot water instead of the vegetable stock. I also added celery based on the reviews.

I love this recipe! I made it the regular way the first time, but another time I had some leftover ham and ham juices, which I added and it was delicious! Either way, it's so easy to make and so satisfying!
This is a solid recipe for a beginner in the kitchen. The directions are easy to follow and easy adjust for food allergies & preferences.

I didn't have all the ingredients but I did use the base recipe. The flavors with the chili powder and Cumin are amazing. I enjoy very spicy foods, so I added some ancho chile powder and some red pepper flakes. I also added red peppers, green beans, and corns because I wanted more vegetables. Overall a very good base and one that I'll definitely make again. Thanks for sharing!
I agree with all the rest of the reviews the soup is delicious. The only difference I used a can of Southwestern corn.
Delicious. Sometimes I throw in an extra can of beans or some shredded chicken.

It turned out delicious! I used fire roasted tomatoes instead of stewed. I only side one can of black beans which I blended with the fire roasted tomatoes. Added celery and used three cups of water with four teaspoons of better than bullion chicken concentrate.

This was an easy soup. I was concerned about blending the black bean with the stewed tomatoes. My very picky 95 yr old mother in law loved it. I added green beans. Next time I’ll add celery as well. Fabulous!!!
